name: Maxilla is law

lead:
"Maxilla is law" is a community maxim claiming the upper jaw (maxilla) shapes the midface, cheeks, under-eye support, nose base and smile more than any other bone, so its forward growth and position largely determine how attractive a face looks.
Believers use it to prioritise midface work: forward-growth approaches such as mewing and palate-focused habits, orthodontic or surgical maxillary advancement, and fillers or implants that mimic midface support. Anatomical reference sources confirm the maxilla's role in the cheek, orbit, palate and nasal floor, but no research ranks it above other features.

paras: In practice people use the idea to evaluate side profile photos for midface projection, discuss non-surgical options such as tongue posture and jaw habits, and read about orthodontic or orthognathic surgery. Surgical options are decided with an oral and maxillofacial surgeon.

Non-surgical claims about reshaping the maxilla in adults are largely untested. Surgical maxillary procedures are major operations with the usual risks of anaesthesia, swelling and bite changes, and are performed by specialists.

chain: Fuller cheeks, better eye support and a more balanced profile
angle.text: Believers use the maxim to focus on midface support, which they say lifts the cheeks, supports the under-eye area and improves the profile. The actual means range from habits to surgery.

lead: "Maxilla is law" is a phrase from looksmaxxing forums asserting that the maxilla, the upper jawbone, is the single most important structure for facial attractiveness. A looksmax.org thread titled with the phrase argues that a well-grown, forward-set maxilla "makes or breaks" attractiveness [1].

The argument rests on anatomy: the maxilla holds the upper teeth and forms the floor of the eye sockets, the roof of the mouth, part of the nasal space and the support of the cheeks. Anatomical references describe it as forming the roof of the mouth, the floor and lateral wall of the nasal cavity and the orbital wall, and attaching laterally to the zygomatic bones [2]. Proponents say an under-developed or recessed maxilla can lead to a sunken or flat midface and to bite problems that alter the smile [1].

Within the community the maxim is used to justify midface-first priorities: forward-growth habits such as mewing, orthodontics, and surgical advancement. Replies in the same thread mention non-surgical routes like mewing and thumb-pulling [1]. No published study ranks the maxilla against other facial features in attractiveness.
infobox: Midface projection, cheek and under-eye support

paras: The saying condenses a view that facial attractiveness is hierarchical, with the upper jaw at the top. In the thread that gave the maxim its form, the original poster describes the maxilla as shaping the midface and cheeks and says growth problems can cause overbite or underbite, a sunken midface and uneven proportions [1].

The maxilla is formed by two bones fused at the intermaxillary suture; its body contains the maxillary sinus and its alveolar process holds the upper teeth. It contributes to the orbit, nasal cavity and palate and articulates with the zygomatic bones [2].

Community members cite the maxim when evaluating profiles and in discussions of mewing and other posture-based approaches; some replies in the thread respond to those suggestions with scepticism [1]. Surgical advancement and orthodontic palate work are discussed as the main structural routes.

No studies found. Studies in orthodontics and maxillofacial surgery examine maxillary growth and advancement for medical indications such as bite correction, but none tests the claim that maxilla position outranks other features in attractiveness.

lore.intro: The maxim appears in looksmax.org threads where users promote the maxilla as the key bone [1].

claims.claim: Maxilla position is the most important factor in facial attractiveness
Non-surgical habits such as mewing can improve the maxilla
